markdown_report:
**Insights from the starting point.** (1) A zero-initialized residual preserves baseline logits for finite branch outputs when added after the existing final normalization. It provides initial equivalence, not subsequent stability [ReZero]. (2) Recent pooling can reinforce current interests but also amplify incidental purchases. With tied embeddings, its added score is exactly recent-item symmetric similarity, potentially reproducing the diagnosed broad-relatedness failure. (3) Electronics/CDs show 21.8%/22.4% sampled training ranking errors. These motivate testing better separation without establishing a validation deficit; near-full embedding rank does not suggest collapse, and missing panels prevent history-sensitivity conclusions.

**Insights from related work.** (1) FSASA combines global/local representations, while MiaSRec questions last-item dominance: compare several recent items with last-item-only pooling. (2) gSASRec motivates an independent calibrated-objective comparison; UFNRec cautions against treating high-scoring unobserved items as verified negatives. (3) FPMC/FOSSIL distinguish source and target embeddings, exposing the symmetry limitation of tied pooling. (4) ReZero explains immediate gate learning and initially blocked branch-only gradients; shared embeddings still learn through existing paths. (5) Paired inference and selection-bias research require identical candidates, limited inspections, and qualified uncertainty statements.

**Framework.** Three directions separate mechanisms: representation horizon, negative-supervision calibration, and adaptive/directional intent fusion. Their minimal experiments are fixed-window residuals, calibrated multi-negative gBCE, and gated or asymmetric residuals. Cross mechanisms only after isolated comparisons. SASRec supplies contextual history modeling; pooling adds a direct similarity path; separate source/target projections allow directional transitions. None observes compatibility, redundancy, or current intent directly.

**Candidates and assessments.** Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=difficulty. Each assessment supplies a positive (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: zero-start recent residual | 2: +controlled extension; −established similarity mechanism | 6: +cheap diagnostic foundation; −limited expressiveness | 6: +recent purpose/style evidence; −may amplify broad similarity | 5: +direct ranking gradients; −inversion reduction unproven | 2: +one scalar; −predictor synchronization |
| B: calibrated multi-negative gBCE | 2: +strong precedent; −existing method | 7: +useful objective baseline; −compute cost | 4: +possible discrimination gains; −no intent mechanism | 8: +targets separation; −false negatives remain | 4: +vectorizable; −calibration details |
| C: learned recency gate | 3: +conditional fusion; −close prior work | 7: +adaptive context; −sparse supervision | 7: +potential intent-shift handling; −intent remains latent | 6: +selective correction; −capacity confound | 5: +compact gate; −additional tuning |
| D: asymmetric recent projection | 3: +directional SASRec extension; −FPMC/FOSSIL precedent | 7: +models directed associations; −extra parameters | 7: +possible useful-addition ranking; −no complement labels | 6: +richer separation; −overfitting risk | 4: +small projection; −initialization and serialization |

**Selected: A**, appropriate at 10% progress as a controlled hypothesis. Use a padding-aware mean of the latest three observed raw item embeddings, including the current observed item: z_t=h_t+αr_t, with one category-specific scalar α initialized exactly to zero. Add it after SASRec’s existing final normalization, with no subsequent normalization; retain the baseline next-item loss. Explicit hypotheses address unsupported broad relatedness and media style/mood drift through stronger recent evidence. Direct next-item supervision also targets Electronics/CDs training-pair inversions. These mechanisms are unverified; symmetric similarity may worsen the first failure, and physical compatibility and redundancy remain unresolved.

Use causal prefixes, exclude padding, and preserve all four models, routing, seeds, splits, and diagnostic interfaces. Serialize window, placement, scaling, and α into the predictor writer. Monitor residual/feature norm ratios and logit changes; do not interpret margin growth alone as improvement. Zero initialization does not prevent shortcut learning through item popularity, embedding norms, or the last item.

Predeclare four attempts: baseline, last-item residual, three-item residual, and previous-two residual excluding the last item. Defer full-prefix, older-prefix, learned-lag, asymmetric, objective, and gate comparisons to a separately declared remaining-budget phase. Cap each initial attempt at 10,800 allocated GPU-seconds, including diagnostics and failures; enforce the shared 43,200-second ceiling across slots. Use the 200-epoch environment default, inspect every 10 completed epochs, patience five inspections, maximum 20 inspections, and select by host-provided macro validation HR@10; ties favor the earlier checkpoint, then baseline, last-item, three-item, previous-two. Declare overrides before execution. If prior search already consumed budget, reduce the plan before launching.

Where the host exposes paired outcomes, report all category scores, wins/losses/both-hit/both-miss counts, and macro differences in percentage points, with paired within-category user-bootstrap 95% intervals. One net hit changes macro HR by 0.125 points. These intervals condition on trained models and fixed sampled candidates; they neither measure seed variability nor correct adaptive selection. Keep every inspection and failed attempt in the ledger. Selection remains the unchanged host HR@10 against 99 negatives; confirmatory claims require untouched final evaluation. No improvement or actual budget consumption is asserted here.

idea.description: Add a zero-initialized, strictly causal recent-window residual after each category-specific SASRec’s existing final normalization: z_t = h_t + alpha * r_t. Here r_t is the padding-aware mean of the latest three observed raw item embeddings, including position t, and alpha is a learned category-specific scalar initialized to zero. Keep the existing objective and compare against baseline, last-item-only, and previous-two-only residuals.
idea.motivation: The hypothesis explicitly targets two user-facing failures: unsupported broad relatedness outranking supported current-purpose matches, and media recommendations drifting across style or mood boundaries. It also targets the observed Electronics/CDs sampled training-pair inversions through the existing next-item supervision. However, the tied-embedding branch adds symmetric similarity rather than identified intent or complementarity, so both user-facing benefits require evidence and could reverse. Missing user panels leave recency dependence unmeasured.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain all four categories and routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, evaluation seed 42, unchanged splits, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Honor SASREC_EPOCHS with the supplied environment default of 200; record any override before training. No extra data or pretrained weights are required. Use raw tied item embeddings without positional embeddings or the encoder’s input sqrt(d) multiplier. Add the branch after the existing final LayerNorm, with no new normalization afterward. Thus the extra candidate score is alpha times the average E_history dot E_candidate, a symmetric Gram similarity. Padding-aware denominators replace three when fewer observations are available. The previous-two control uses offsets one and two relative to t; it must return zero when no earlier observations exist. Construct the scalar module after baseline initialization, without additional random draws. Alpha is signed and unconstrained; initialize it exactly to zero and place it in an explicit no-weight-decay optimizer group using the baseline learning rate, betas, and epsilon. Preserve every existing optimizer group and log all resolved settings. Initial equality requires identical baseline weights, finite branch outputs, and identical stochastic state. Alpha can learn immediately; shared embeddings continue receiving baseline encoder/output gradients, although the residual contribution to their gradient starts at zero. Initial equivalence does not guarantee stable later updates. Monitor alpha, branch and baseline norms, abs(alpha)*norm(r)/max(norm(h), epsilon), and candidate-logit differences on a fixed training-only diagnostic sample. Report scale and ranking changes separately. Match baseline and variant checkpoint inspection budgets. Predeclare four attempts including baseline, each capped at 10,800 allocated GPU-seconds with training, diagnostics, debugging, and failures included; enforce the global ceiling across four slots and deduct prior consumption before scheduling. Inspect every 10 completed epochs, use five-inspection patience and at most 20 inspections under the 200-epoch setting, and select by host-returned macro validation HR@10. Ties favor earlier checkpoints and then baseline, last-item, three-item, previous-two. Do not recreate host candidates or fabricate outcomes when unavailable. Store inspected outcomes when exposed by the host; report paired category counts, scores, percentage-point differences, and paired user-bootstrap intervals as exploratory and conditional on fixed models/candidates. Log failures, pruning, overrides, selection opportunities, and actual GPU consumption. Do not claim selection-corrected significance. Write the identical module and configuration into the predictor writer and load alpha in every category checkpoint. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and its metrics/metric_definitions return contract. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module; view.log2feats returns augmented features, view.item_emb remains the tied table, and predict_score uses those same features. Do not consume the live training iterator merely to obtain diagnostic examples or fabricate missing panels. Use only public histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions; ratings, reviews, prices, stores, item category labels, and simulator traits remain unavailable. Full-prefix and older-prefix controls, learned lag weights, asymmetric source projections, calibrated gBCE, and adaptive gates remain deferred experiments requiring a declared budget. Shuffling only the uniformly pooled branch cannot test order sensitivity because its output is permutation invariant.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
from torch import nn

class RecentResidual(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, window=3, exclude_current=False):
        super().__init__()
        self.window = int(window)
        self.exclude_current = bool(exclude_current)
        if self.window < 1:
            raise ValueError('window must be positive')
        self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(()))

    def forward(self, baseline_features, sequence, item_emb):
        # sequence: B x L, left-padded with zero.
        # baseline_features: original SASRec output AFTER existing final LN.
        valid = sequence.ne(0)
        values = item_emb(sequence)  # raw tied embeddings, no sqrt(d) scaling
        values = values.masked_fill(~valid.unsqueeze(-1), 0)
        # Accumulate in float32 for the normal float32/mixed-precision baseline.
        accum = values.float()
        sums = torch.cat([
            accum.new_zeros(accum.size(0), 1, accum.size(2)),
            accum.cumsum(dim=1)
        ], dim=1)
        counts = torch.cat([
            accum.new_zeros(accum.size(0), 1),
            valid.to(accum.dtype).cumsum(dim=1)
        ], dim=1)
        end = torch.arange(1, sequence.size(1) + 1, device=sequence.device)
        if self.exclude_current:
            end = end - 1
        start = (end - self.window).clamp_min(0)
        recent_sum = sums[:, end] - sums[:, start]
        recent_count = counts[:, end] - counts[:, start]
        recent = recent_sum / recent_count.clamp_min(1).unsqueeze(-1)
        recent = recent.to(baseline_features.dtype)
        result = baseline_features + self.alpha * recent
        return result.masked_fill(~valid.unsqueeze(-1), 0)

# Instantiate AFTER the unchanged baseline modules and their initialization.
# Primary: RecentResidual(window=3, exclude_current=False).
# Controls: window=1/current included; window=2/current excluded.
# Baseline uses the original model without the branch.
# Add alpha to a separate optimizer group: same baseline lr/betas/eps,
# weight_decay=0; preserve existing parameter groups.
# log2feats: original SASRec computation -> existing final LN -> residual.
# Use augmented features consistently for loss, prediction, and diagnostics.
# Save window, exclude_current, placement, scaling, optimizer settings, alpha.
# Predictor writer emits this same definition and category routing.
# Keep the original next-item objective and all input splits unchanged.
# Host supplies selection HR@10; no replacement evaluator is constructed.
# Log each checkpoint inspection and all allocated single-GPU time.
# If exposed: d_c[u] = int(new_hit_c[u]) - int(baseline_hit_c[u]).
# delta_macro = mean_c(mean_u(d_c[u])).
# Bootstrap user indices independently within each category, preserving pairing;
# compute macro delta for each replicate and report percentile 95% intervals.
# Label these intervals exploratory, conditional on fixed trained models/candidates.

originality.positive: Zero-start fusion offers a clean controlled extension that exposes the incremental value of a direct recent-history path.
originality.negative: Recent-item pooling is established, and tied scoring reduces exactly to symmetric similarity. ReZero supplies the zero-gate precedent; FOSSIL already combines pooled history and recent actions.

future_potential.positive: A successful controlled comparison could establish a cheap foundation for directional projections, adaptive horizons, or independently tested objective changes.
future_potential.negative: The mechanism cannot identify current purpose, compatibility, substitution, or redundancy, and may strengthen the same broad similarity shortcut identified by users.

code_difficulty.positive: Prefix-sum pooling adds linear sequence work, one scalar per category, and no external dependencies or random initialization.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful placement, optimizer grouping, predictor generation, diagnostic consistency, and budget accounting require care; running the complete evaluation protocol adds operational work.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention recommendation baseline and contextual selection of relevant historical actions.
limitations: Does not explicitly identify current purpose or physical compatibility; an added recency branch must demonstrate utility beyond its existing contextual modeling.

related_work.title: FSASA
contributions: Combines global SASRec representations with local session-aware representations using GRU weighting.
limitations: Does not establish the best local horizon or gains on these four pinned categories.

related_work.title: MiaSRec
contributions: Uses item-centered intent representations and dynamic selection, motivating alternatives to last-item dominance.
limitations: Its intent machinery is more complex than the initial residual experiment and does not validate a three-item window here.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Attributes SASRec weaknesses to sampled-BCE overconfidence and motivates calibrated multi-negative objectives.
limitations: Calibration and negative counts need controlled evaluation within the shared compute budget; reported findings do not establish gains on this benchmark.

related_work.title: UFNRec
contributions: Uses teacher soft labels and consistency regularization to address suspected false negatives.
limitations: Teacher training adds cost, and unobserved items remain uncertain negatives in this task.

related_work.title: ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Introduces zero-initialized residual gates and explains identity initialization and gradient propagation.
limitations: Whole-network results do not guarantee stability or recommendation gains for a residual added to SASRec with tied embeddings and existing normalization.

related_work.title: On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture
contributions: Analyzes how normalization placement affects Transformer initialization gradients.
limitations: Its assumptions do not establish stability for this particular post-normalization recommendation residual.

related_work.title: Fixup Initialization: Residual Learning Without Normalization
contributions: Uses depth-dependent initialization to control residual-network functional updates.
limitations: A zero initial scalar alone does not inherit its update-scale guarantees.

related_work.title: Fusing Similarity Models with Markov Chains for Sparse Sequential Recommendation
contributions: FOSSIL combines normalized history pooling and weighted recent actions, using distinct source and target embeddings.
Discusses FPMC’s combination of persistent preferences and asymmetric first-order transitions.
limitations: These precedents reduce the originality of recent pooling; directed transitions still do not establish complementarity or current intent.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains how sampled ranking metrics can differ from full-catalog comparisons.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator; results must remain explicitly described as HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives.

related_work.title: Fay and Lumbard: Matched-Proportion Inference
contributions: Provides methods for inference on differences in paired binary outcomes, relevant to paired per-user hit comparisons.
limitations: Paired outcome inference does not capture training-seed variability or remove adaptive model-selection bias.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains overfitting to model-selection criteria and resulting performance-estimation bias.
limitations: Ordinary bootstrap intervals around the selected validation winner do not correct this bias; checkpoint and trial selection must be disclosed.
